subject: Oceanside RFI: Data residency, retention, and deletion (hosted API)
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura@oceansideanalytics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Oceanside Legal <legal@oceansideanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: Data residency, retention & deletion - hosted API

Hi Neha / Karthik,

Thanks for taking this RFI. Attached is our standard security questionnaire (Oceanside_Security_RFI_v3.pdf). We're specifically focused on three items for your hosted API:

- Where customer data is persisted geographically and how we can verify it.
- Retention windows for request logs, embeddings, and any backups/snapshots.
- Deletion guarantees (time to complete, evidence artifacts) and how erasures propagate through caches/backups.

Can you provide a short written response and any supporting evidence or artifacts we can include in our compliance package? We'd like to share the answers with our security team and may follow up for a short technical call.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Head of Security Ops
Oceanside Analytics
[Attachment: Oceanside_Security_RFI_v3.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@oceansideanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Data residency, retention & deletion - hosted API

Laura — appreciate the doc. We've prepared an initial set of responses and a short evidence pack; attaching the working draft (HostedAPI-Residency-Answers-oc.docx). Key points up front:

- Residency: Customer data for the hosted API is stored in the region the customer selects at account creation (US east / US west / EU west currently). We operate region-specific S3 buckets and VPCs; metadata that indicates region is embedded in object paths and access logs.
- Retention: Request logs (redacted request metadata, throttling metrics) are retained for 90 days by default; embeddings and model-generated outputs are retained for 30 days unless an enterprise contract opts into longer retention. We can offer custom retention windows via Dedicated/Private plans.
- Deletion: On erasure request we delete active objects and metadata within 30 days; ephemeral caches and KV caches are marked for eviction immediately and purged within 72 hours. Backups/snapshots are retained on a rolling schedule; final snapshot deletion occurs within the next scheduled retention pruning cycle (within 30 days) and we provide an attestation once complete.

I've included short evidence pointers in the doc (config snippets, S3 path examples, and a snapshot removal timeline). Kimberly — can you review the deletion wording below and confirm we can commit to 30 days for cross-region purges in our hosted SLA?

Next steps: If that aligns, I'll upload the evidence artifacts to the shared drive link and schedule a 30-minute technical Q&A with your engineering team.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: HostedAPI-Residency-Answers-oc.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Data residency, retention & deletion - hosted API

Neha — quick pass from Legal/Privacy POV. I made two suggested edits in the doc:

- Clarify that "request logs" are pseudonymized (IP and PII hashes) before long-term storage; raw request payloads are not preserved beyond short-term processing unless explicitly logged for debugging with customer consent.
- Change wording from "within 30 days" to "up to 30 days" for snapshot deletion propagation to avoid implying deterministic under-30-day deletion during exceptional operational recovery windows.

Suggested contract language for deletion clause (can be pasted into answers):
"Upon a verified erasure request, Redwood will initiate deletion of customer data from active stores and caching layers immediately and will complete deletion from backups and scheduled snapshots within a commercially reasonable period not to exceed 30 days, subject to standard backup retention windows and applicable law."

I'll attach a redlined snippet to the drive after this. Karthik — from an infra standpoint, we should include the ephemeral architecture diagram (redwood-ephemeral-architecture.png) to show how KV caches are isolated per-tenant.

Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura@oceansideanalytics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Oceanside Legal <legal@oceansideanalytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Data residency, retention & deletion - hosted API

Thanks — the draft is helpful. A few follow-ups from our legal team:

1) Proof of deletion: For compliance we need an auditable artifact after erasure requests (audit record + timestamped confirmation). Can you provide a sample confirmation format?
2) Cache behavior: We understand KV caches are tenant-isolated. What guarantees do you offer that caches don't persist beyond the stated window (we'd like a maximum of 7 days for any cached model state unless explicitly configured otherwise).
3) Backups: Please confirm whether region-specific backups are encrypted with a region-bound KMS key and whether key rotation affects the ability to decrypt older snapshots for deletion verification.

We may request a short follow-up call after the artifacts are uploaded.

Best,
Laura
[Oceanside_Security_RFI_v3.pdf attached previously]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@oceansideanalytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Oceanside Legal <legal@oceansideanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Data residency, retention & deletion - hosted API

Laura — thanks for the follow-ups. Short answers below plus links to the evidence pack I've uploaded: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Oceanside/RFI-evidence

1) Proof of deletion: We provide a machine-readable erasure confirmation (PDF + JSON record) that includes: request id, affected object keys/prefixes (redacted as necessary), timestamps for each stage (initiation, cache purge, active-store deletion, backup pruning), and the signing identity (Redwood operations ticket id). Example confirmation is in the drive (deletion_confirmation_example.json + deletion_confirmation_example.pdf).

2) Cache guarantees: KV and prefix caches are tenant-scoped; eviction is immediate on verified erasure request and we guarantee removal from in-memory caches within 24 hours and from on-disk cache shards within 72 hours. For hosted customers, default max TTL for caches is 7 days; we document this in the evidence pack and it is configurable for Dedicated/Private deployments. The ephemeral architecture diagram (redwood-ephemeral-architecture.png) is in the drive.

3) Backups and KMS: Backups are region-specific and encrypted with customer-region KMS keys managed by Redwood. Key rotation is performed with retention-aware procedures that preserve decryption capability for the backup window; rotation does not block deletion verification. We include snapshot manifests and KMS key identifiers in the evidence pack to help your security team validate.

Next steps: I propose a 30-minute technical session (engineers only) to walk through the architecture and one example deletion confirmation. I'm available Thu 08/28 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 08/29 13:00-14:00 PT — which works best?

Thanks — attaching the evidence manifest and the redlined deletion clause Kimberly suggested.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0142
[Attachments uploaded to drive: deletion_confirmation_example.pdf, deletion_confirmation_example.json, redwood-ephemeral-architecture.png]
